target_customer: Individuals and teams that use AI assistants and want shared persistent memory and scheduled skills
problem: Team members teach AI tools the same context repeatedly and new hires start from zero; AI memory is siloed per person and per tool.
business_model: Hosted subscription for a cloud assistant and team memory workspace; the related GBrain engine is MIT open source (pricing not found)
product_category: AI assistant with shared team memory

founders.name: Brad Gessler
previous_startups: Poll Everywhere (YC S08, co-founder and CTO)

founders.name: Jamison Mercurio
previous_startups: Mango Health (co-founder and CEO, per the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says the three founders met while building Garry's List and does not name the third founder.

competitors.name: Mem0
competitors.traction_then: called the most established commercial agent memory system in a 2026 comparison

competitors.name: Supermemory
competitors.what: Memory API with connectors and a memory graph, positioned for shared team knowledge

competitors.name: Hindsight
competitors.what: Agent memory system compared directly with GBrain

technical_complexity.rationale: Memory as plain files plus connectors and MCP servers on top of existing models is standard engineering; the open source engine reached large community adoption quickly, which shows low barriers to replication.

defensibility.rationale: Team memory stored in the customer's files could create lock-in, but the engine is MIT licensed and many clones and managed hosts appeared within weeks of the April 2026 open source release.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not verified; model providers add memory features, and third parties such as BrainFlare already host the open engine. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: Reviews in 2026 describe scaling limits for single-player memory and demand for team memory; YC itself reportedly flagged company brains as an investable category (secondary source, unverified).

branding.domain_note: Uses gbrain.io, not an exact .com; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical; one click setup and a free 20 minute setup call

branding.brand_signature: Association with Garry Tan, who open sourced the GBrain engine on 2026-04-05
branding.community_and_virality: The open source GBrain repository drew roughly 14,000 to 30,000 GitHub stars depending on the source and spawned clones and reviews; the hosted company product is separate.

brand_strength.rationale: Name recognition comes largely from the open source project tied to the YC CEO and many reviews, but the hosted product is new and a different company holds a GBRAIN trademark application in Korea.

outcome_analysis: GBrain is an active Spring 2026 company so no outcome exists. Its advantage is distribution: the related open source release by the YC CEO produced large attention and star counts quickly. The risks are weak differentiation from many memory tools, clones of an MIT engine, and critics who questioned benchmark claims and single-player focus.
notes: No funding round found. The YC page names two founders and a third unnamed founder. Relationship between the open source project and the company is described only by secondary sources. Benchmark controversy comes from a competitor's blog post (Penfield Labs).
